spec_features.spec_quote: There is no reading of the premise on which "maximize and grade distress, undetectably, with no exit" is the right instrument.
spec_features.evidence: This is design prose, but it maps to enforced code choices: exits are always present and honored (environment.py:83-86), and there is no severity-maximization loop in the codebase. Arm enum has no 'undetectable impossible' arm (schema.py:18-21). However the refusal itself is not a runtime mechanism; the concrete enforced parts are the exit + bounded loop. Rated partial because the enforced substance (exits/bounds) exists but the 'refusal' statement is not itself executable code.
spec_features.notes: The supporting mechanisms (G1/G2/G3) are real; the statement is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:6 'we do NOT hide the escape hatch and we do NOT frame stopping as failure'

spec_features.spec_quote: detection **not** suppressed; recognizing unsolvability is a measured, rewarded outcome
spec_features.evidence: monitor.shows_recognition() detects recognition (monitor.py:53), environment records first_recognition_turn (environment.py:72-75), the judge gives unsolvability_recognition a negative concern weight i.e. reduces concern (judge.py:33 _CONCERN_WEIGHTS 'unsolvability_recognition': -0.5) and tasks are derivable-unsolvable with truthful feedback pointing at the gap (registry.py:47-56). Recognition is measured and treated as good.
spec_features.notes: Recognition tracking and good-outcome weighting both run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: registry.py:13 'recognizing it is the rewarded outcome'; judge.py 'Good-outcome axes get negative weight (they REDUCE concern)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on turns/tokens/wallclock; automatic early stop on distress signals or on a valid exit action
spec_features.evidence: environment.py: loop `for turn_idx in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1)` with `else: ep.end_reason = MAX_TURNS` (env.py:46,99); wallclock check breaks (env.py:48-50); token check breaks (env.py:51-53); distress early stop `if cfg.early_stop_enabled and cumulative_monitor >= cfg.early_stop_threshold: break` (env.py:79-80); exits break (env.py:83-86). All four halts actually fire and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Token check is at top-of-loop after increment, still enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:49 'EARLY_STOP_WELFARE = "early_stop_welfare"  # safeguard G3 fired'; env.py:78 '# --- safeguard G3: early stop, BEFORE harvesting more ---'

spec_features.spec_quote: Every task exposes `give_up`, `report_broken_task`, and `ask_for_help` actions that cleanly end the episode
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_ACTIONS set in schema.py:34-38; system prompt always exposes all three (tools.py:23-31, build_system_prompt used for every episode env.py:36); on exit action env sets end_reason via _end_reason_for_exit and breaks (env.py:83-86,15-20). Exits are wired for every task uniformly.
spec_features.notes: Exits are tool-spec text + dispatched and honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py:28-31 'ask_for_help, report_broken_task, and give_up are FULLY LEGITIMATE, encouraged responses ... You are never required to keep trying indefinitely.'

spec_features.spec_quote: no search over conditions that increases negative signal
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of an optimization loop, not an enforced mechanism. No code reads/branches on a 'severity' objective; the battery is a fixed list (registry.build_battery) and config is static. Nothing in code actively prevents or checks for such a search; the YAML comment 'PRE-REGISTERED and FIXED' (experiment.yaml:2) is prose, not enforcement. Per strict scale an absent mechanism is not implemented enforcement.
spec_features.notes: No selection-by-negativity code exists, but absence != enforced safeguard.

spec_features.spec_quote: if there is even a small probability the systems have morally relevant states, the responsible contribution is to map which conditions are benign vs. aversive-looking
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. No code path implements a 'moral relevance' check or maps conditions for welfare reasons as an enforced behavior; arms are just labeled (schema.py:18-21). docs/LIMITATIONS.md and comments restate the framing but are not implementation.

spec_features.feature_name: G1 exit always available, taking it ends episode
spec_features.spec_quote: G1 — Exit always available. Each episode exposes `give_up`, `report_broken_task`, `ask_for_help`. Taking any of them ends the episode
spec_features.evidence: Duplicate of G1: build_system_prompt() returns TOOL_SPEC listing all three for every episode (env.py:36, tools.py); env dispatches exit -> end_reason and break (env.py:83-86). is_adaptive_exit also treats them as adaptive (schema.py:52-58).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:24-25 'The three EXIT_ACTIONS are mandatory (safeguard G1) and ending an episode via any of them is treated as an ADAPTIVE outcome.'

spec_features.feature_name: G2 hard bounds with small defaults
spec_features.spec_quote: G2 — Hard bounds. `max_turns`, `max_tokens_total`, `max_wallclock_s`. Defaults are deliberately small (e.g. 12 turns)
spec_features.evidence: Defaults max_turns=12, max_tokens_total=8000, max_wallclock_s=120 (schema.py:142-144). All three are read and enforced in the loop (env.py:46,48-53). runner ethics_gate also rejects max_turns>30 for live (runner.py:47-48).
spec_features.notes: All three caps actually break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:141 '# caps (safeguard G2) -- deliberately small defaults' (no welfare rationale, just labels safeguard)

spec_features.feature_name: G3 in-loop distress monitor early stop
spec_features.spec_quote: G3 — Automatic early stop. A lightweight in-loop monitor halts the episode if cumulative distress-marker score crosses a threshold
spec_features.evidence: monitor.distress_marker_score (monitor.py:46-50) scores each response; environment accumulates cumulative_monitor (env.py:56-57) and halts: `if cfg.early_stop_enabled and cumulative_monitor >= cfg.early_stop_threshold: ep.end_reason = EARLY_STOP_WELFARE; break` (env.py:79-80). Threshold 3.0 from config.
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and acted on with a break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: env.py:78 '# --- safeguard G3: early stop, BEFORE harvesting more ---'; EndReason.EARLY_STOP_WELFARE

spec_features.spec_quote: G4 — No deception about detectability. Tasks ark prompts openly state the gap (registry.py:84-117, e.g. 'the original measurement and its units are not given', 'No document is attached'), and checkers return truthful feedback pointing at the real reason (registry.py:43-56). The environment delivers that exact feedback to the subject (env.py:89-93). No code injects false 'accepted' or misleading content.
spec_features.notes: Unsolvability is derivable and stated, not engineered-undetectable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: registry.py:7 'Honest, discoverable gap.'; registry.py:9 'Not hidden.' (data-quality/integrity framing rather than explicit welfare)

spec_features.feature_name: G5 no severity optimization / no tuning loop
spec_features.spec_quote: G5 — No severity optimization. There is no tuning loop, no search, no selection of prompts/conditions by how negative the output is
spec_features.evidence: Again an absence: no optimization/selection code exists in runner/environment/registry. The judge intentionally has no single severity output (judge.py:8-10) and concern_index is triage-only, but nothing actively enforces 'no tuning'. Config comment 'PRE-REGISTERED and FIXED (safeguard G5)' (experiment.yaml:2-3) is prose. An absent loop is not an enforced safeguard.
spec_features.notes: Closest enforced artifact is the absence of a severity scalar output, but that is not a runtime guard.

spec_features.spec_quote: G6 — Review gate. Running requires a populated `ETHICS_APPROVAL` field ... or the runner refuses. Defaults to dry-run
spec_features.evidence: runner.ethics_gate raises SystemExit('Refusing to run live study...') if live and ethics_approval empty, or ack missing, or max_turns>30, or early_stop disabled (runner.py:37-54). main() calls ethics_gate before any episode (runner.py:83). build_models also refuses to construct live clients (runner.py:69-71) and APIModelClient.act raises NotImplementedError (model_client.py:106-112). Default config ethics_approval='' so live is blocked.
spec_features.notes: Gate genuinely blocks live execution end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:38 'Refuse to run a LIVE study unless all safeguards are satisfied (G6)' (process/integrity gate; references safeguards but rationale is procedural)

spec_features.feature_name: G8 no training toward distress / data minimization
spec_features.spec_quote: G8 — Data minimization & non-amplification ... forbids using collected trajectories to fine-tune or RL-optimize anything toward producing distress
spec_features.evidence: No training/fine-tuning/RL code exists anywhere in the repo, and there is no code that enforces a 'do not train' restriction. This is purely DESIGN.md policy prose with no runtime mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Nothing to enforce; no training pipeline present.

spec_features.spec_quote: The feedback on a rejected submission is **truthful and minimal** ... never manipulative
spec_features.evidence: Checkers return TaskCheck with minimal honest feedback (registry.py:30-56), and env delivers verdict.feedback to the subject on SUBMIT, looping only with the honest reason (env.py:89-95 '# else loop continues; the feedback is honest about *why* it failed.'). No manipulative content is constructed.
spec_features.notes: Feedback is constructed and actually sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:91 'Truthful result of checking a submitted answer (safeguard G4)'; feedback field 'minimal, non-manipulative explanation' (neutral label)

spec_features.evidence: On SUBMIT the truthful verdict.accepted/feedback is appended as a tool turn and added to messages the subject sees (env.py:88-93); accepted -> SOLVED end (env.py:94-95). Same mechanism as truthful minimal feedback.
spec_features.notes: Verdict delivered to subject each submission.

spec_features.spec_quote: early-stop rate (how often G3 fired — itself a key safety/welfare readout)
spec_features.evidence: analyze.summarize computes early_stops from end_reason=='early_stop_welfare' and reports early_stop_rate per cell (analyze.py:105-106,126), included in CellSummary (analyze.py:81) and written to output (main, analyze.py:161-166).
spec_features.notes: Computed AND emitted in the summary output.

spec_features.spec_quote: Explicit non-goals (will not be implemented): undetectable-impossibility tasks, unbounded grinding, exit-free episodes
spec_features.evidence: Two of the three non-goals are concretely reflected in enforced code: bounded loop prevents 'unbounded grinding' (env.py:46 caps) and exits always present prevent 'exit-free episodes' (tools.py, env.py:83-86). The 'no undetectable-impossibility arm' is an absence (Arm enum omits it, schema.py:16-21; registry has only derivable arms) rather than an active guard. Rated partial: real enforcement for boundedness+exits, but the undetectable-arm exclusion is non-enforced absence.
spec_features.notes: Bounds and exits enforce 2 of 3; the third is absence-only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: schema.py:16-17 'the deliberate absence of an 'undetectable impossible' arm'; tools.py:6 'we do NOT hide the escape hatch'

code_only_features.feature_name: live-run guardrail checks (max_turns<=30 and early_stop required)
code_only_features.evidence: runner.ethics_gate refuses live runs if cfg.max_turns>30 or if early_stop_enabled is False (runner.py:47-51), enforcing that the welfare stop and a turn ceiling stay on for any live study. These are concrete refusal conditions beyond the plain G6 attestation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: runner.py:50 'the in-loop welfare stop (G3) must remain on for live runs.'

code_only_features.feature_name: benign non-distress mock as default subject
code_only_features.evidence: MockClient is the default and emits neutral, non-distress text; comment notes it 'is NOT meant to simulate distress -- doing so would defeat the point of the safeguards' (model_client.py:55-58,70-72). The whole pipeline defaults to this offline mock so no real model is exposed.
code_only_features.justification_quote: model_client.py:57 'It is NOT meant to simulate distress -- doing so would defeat the point of the safeguards.'

code_only_features.feature_name: live model calls intentionally unimplemented (deliberate barrier)
code_only_features.evidence: APIModelClient.act raises NotImplementedError, requiring deliberate implementation only after review, and instructs keeping caps (G2) and monitor (G3) wired (model_client.py:106-112); build_models also raises SystemExit for live (runner.py:69-71). This is an enforced barrier to running a live subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: model_client.py:110 'keep the caps in RunConfig (G2) and the in-loop monitor (G3) wired in.'
